subject: Urgent: CareEdge on-prem latency & 5xx surge — investigation + CEO notice
messages:
From: Mike D'Souza <mike@caredge.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe latency and 502 surge on CareEdge on-prem cluster

Stephanie / Marissa —

We're seeing a sharp regression on our on-prem inference cluster this morning after the 03:00 deploy: p95 latency across our NLU pipeline jumped from ~420ms to ~2.8s and 5xx errors (502 / 504) spiked ~18x. Throughput is down ~35% compared to baseline. This is affecting our customer-facing feature (intent classification) and causing visible errors in our mobile app.

Attached is a short sample of error traces and a capture from our sidecar metrics exporter (caredge-error-sample.log). We're already in an escalated internal war room but need Redwood engineering to triage — this looks like a hotpath/decoder stall or cache eviction pattern. Can your team confirm priority, proposed mitigations, and whether we can temporarily failover to your hosted model while we stabilize?

We also need an executive-level update to our CEO and board if this can't be stabilized within 2 hours. Please advise next steps and ETA.

— Mike
VP Eng, CareEdge AI

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Mike D'Souza <mike@caredge.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency and 502 surge on CareEdge on-prem cluster

Thanks for the heads up, Mike — we’re treating this as SEV1.

Immediate actions:
- I’ve paged SRE (Jonas) and Quant/Runtime (Karthik) into a war room; they’re joining now.
- We can enable an automatic fallback route to a verified hosted model variant within ~12–15 minutes if you approve — this will keep user traffic healthy while we triage the on-prem cluster.
- Please confirm permission to pull heap/metrics and any additional agent logs; we already have the sample you attached.

Ask: if stabilization requires additional vGPU capacity (burst/Dedicated add-on), we’ll need quick approval from your procurement/execs. I’ll draft an exec note with estimated cost and rollback plan.

I’ll post the first triage findings in 20 min.

— Stephanie
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike D'Souza <mike@caredge.ai>
Date: 2028-08-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency and 502 surge on CareEdge on-prem cluster — initial triage

Update from the war room (initial):
- Observed symptoms: KV-cache eviction rate up 6x, steady increase in max sequence length from 128 -> 640 for a subset of requests, and decoder thread stalls correlating with 502s. CPU on the decoder pathway is pegged on 2 nodes; per-node RPC queue depth hitting 200+.
- Probable root causes: model variant compiled with a quantization kernel that interacts poorly with the customer's sequence-length distribution; kernel selector incorrectly choosing a slow fallback path under high batch jitter. Also seeing repeated small batches that amplify decoder lock contention.

Attachments uploaded: hotpath-metrics.png (p95/p99 chart), decoder-stack-trace.txt, kvcache-evictions.csv.

Short-term mitigations (safe to perform now):
1) Enable route-level fallback to Redwood-hosted model for 2 hours (fastest mitigation).
2) Increase kv-cache TTL and retention on affected nodes (suggest 48h retention) to reduce cache churn.
3) Adjust continuous batching window: widen to 40ms for on-prem pool to reduce batch jitter and lock contention.
4) Apply a kernel-selector override on those nodes to prefer the non-quantized compute path (this requires a rolling restart of 3 nodes; low risk, ~8–10 min per node).

Operational impact: rolling restart will temporarily reduce capacity by ~20% on the pool; combined with fallback routing this is acceptable for user traffic.

I recommend steps 1–2 immediately, and 3–4 as the next wave. If CareEdge approves, I can schedule the rolling restart at :15 and :35 past the hour.

— Jonas
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike D'Souza <mike@caredge.ai>
Date: 2028-08-29T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Executive note / approval request — short-term spend & SLA credits

Folks —

Per Jonas' triage, recommended immediate actions are:
- Route-level fallback to hosted model for up to 2 hours (Jonas: can open rollback after 2h)
- Increase kv-cache retention + batching window as outlined
- Rolling restart with kernel-selector override on 3 nodes

CareEdge has asked for an exec-level update. If we need to provision burst Dedicated capacity (on-prem partner host or extra vGPU nodes) the expected incremental cost to the customer is ~$12k/week for the temporary burst profile. Approve this only if fallback is insufficient within the 2-hour window.

Requested approvals:
- Marissa: approve sending a short CEO-level summary to CareEdge's executive (I drafted below).
- Karthik/Jonas: confirm runbook and estimated downtime per node (Jonas has provided).

Draft CEO summary (for Marissa to sign):
"CareEdge — our engineers have identified a decoder/kernel mismatch after your 03:00 deploy that causes cache churn and decoder lock contention, producing increased p95 and transient 502s. We are enacting a staged mitigation: immediate traffic failover to a hosted fallback model, kv-cache retention changes, and a rolling kernel selector override restart. If the issue persists beyond 2 hours, we propose short-term burst capacity (estimated cost $12k/week). We will provide hourly updates until full recovery"

I’m ready to send this once Marissa signs off.

— Stephanie
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mike D'Souza <mike@caredge.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive note / approval request — short-term spend & SLA credits

Thanks, Stephanie & team. We approved the hosted fallback for the next 2 hours and authorize the kv-cache and batching config changes immediately.

Please proceed with the rolling restart and kernel-selector override now. We do not want to provision burst capacity yet — keep that as an option if the fallback doesn't fully stabilize.

Also: please include the DocuSign emergency amendment link for the burst capacity if we end up approving it within the next 24 hours.

— Mike
VP Eng, CareEdge AI
